<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As a result of these facts, Schlumberger determined that it was more likely than not that the fair value of certain of its reporting units were less than their carrying value.&#160;&#160;Therefore, Schlumberger performed an interim goodwill impairment test as of August 31, 2019.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of August 31, 2019, Schlumberger had <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000512" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_20190831_20190831" decimals="INF">17</ix:nonFraction> reporting units with goodwill balances aggregating $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000513" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_20190831" decimals="-8" scale="9">25.0</ix:nonFraction> billion.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger determined that the fair value of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000514" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbSevenReportingUnitsMember_20190831_20190831" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">seven</ix:nonFraction> of its reporting units, representing approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000515" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbSevenReportingUnitsMember_20190831" decimals="-8" scale="9">13.8</ix:nonFraction> billion of the goodwill, was substantially in excess of their carrying value.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger performed a detailed quantitative impairment assessment of the remaining <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000516" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbTenReportingUnitsMember_20190831_20190831" decimals="INF">10</ix:nonFraction> reporting units, which represented $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000517" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbTenReportingUnitsMember_20190831" decimals="-8" scale="9">11.2</ix:nonFraction> billion of goodwill. <p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000459_dcnt_9cc888f0-221a-4d84-a673-644e2a567e49" continuedAt="F_000459_dcnt_ebadf475-0ad4-43c8-8764-c98f8aa021bb">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Following the $8.8 billion goodwill impairment charge relating to these nine reporting units, only three had a remaining goodwill balance.&#160;&#160;These <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000520" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbThreeReportingUnitsMember_20190831_20190831" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">three</ix:nonFraction> reporting units had goodwill balances which ranged between $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000521" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbThreeReportingUnitsMember_20190831" decimals="-8" scale="9">0.4</ix:nonFraction> billion and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000522" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbThreeReportingUnitsMember_20190831" decimals="-8" scale="9">0.6</ix:nonFraction> billion and aggregated to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000523" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbThreeReportingUnitsMember_20190831" decimals="-8" scale="9">1.5</ix:nonFraction> billion as of August 31, 2019. The <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000524" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbReportingUnitOneMember_20190831_20190831" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">ten</ix:nonFraction>th reporting unit, which was determined not to be impaired, had $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000525" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbReportingUnitOneMember_20190831" decimals="-8" scale="9">0.9</ix:nonFraction> billion of goodwill.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger primarily used the income approach to estimate the fair value of its reporting units, but also considered the market approach to validate the results.&#160;&#160;The income approach estimates the fair value by discounting each reporting unit&#8217;s estimated future cash flows using Schlumberger&#8217;s estimate of the discount rate, or expected return, that a marketplace participant would have required as of the valuation date.&#160;&#160;The market approach includes the use of comparative multiples to corroborate the discounted cash flow results.&#160;&#160;The market approach involves significant judgement involved in the selection of the appropriate peer group companies and valuation multiples.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Some of the more significant assumptions inherent in the income approach include the estimated future net annual cash flows for each reporting unit and the discount rate.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger selected the assumptions used in the discounted cash flow projections using historical data supplemented by current and anticipated market conditions and estimated growth rates.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#8217;s estimates are based upon assumptions believed to be reasonable.&#160;&#160;However, given the inherent uncertainty in determining the assumptions underlying a discounted cash flow analysis, actual results may differ from those used in Schlumberger&#8217;s valuations which could result in additional impairment charges in the future.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Substantially all</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> of the charges recorded during the third quarter of 2019 will not result in any future cash outflows. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the third quarter of 2019, Schlumberger&#8217;s Board of Directors announced the appointment of a new Chief Executive Officer.&#160;&#160;As the new Chief Executive Officer further develops and implements his strategy, it may result in additional restructuring charges in future periods.&#160;&#160;Furthermore, Schlumberger may be required to record additional impairment charges if industry conditions deteriorate.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the second quarter of 2018, Schlumberger recorded a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000558" name="slb:ChargesAndCreditsPretax" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapIncomeStatementLocationAxis_slbImpairmentsAndOtherMember_us-gaapRestructuringCostAndReserveAxis_us-gaapEmployeeSeveranceMember_20180401_20180630" decimals="-6" scale="6">184</ix:nonFraction> million pretax charge ($<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000559" name="slb:ChargesAndCredits" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapIncomeStatementLocationAxis_slbImpairmentsAndOtherMember_us-gaapRestructuringCostAndReserveAxis_us-gaapEmployeeSeveranceMember_20180401_20180630" decimals="-6" scale="6">164</ix:nonFraction> million after-tax) associated with headcount reductions, primarily to further streamline its support cost structure.&#160;&#160;This charge is classified in <span style="font-style:italic;">Impairments &#38; other</span> in the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Statement of Income (Loss)</span>.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">10.&#160;&#160; <span style="text-decoration:underline;">Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities</span> </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is exposed to market risks related to fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates and interest rates.&#160; To mitigate these risks, Schlumberger utilizes derivative instruments.&#160; Schlumberger does not enter into derivative transactions for speculative purposes. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Interest Rate Risk </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is subject to interest rate risk on its debt and its investment portfolio.&#160; Schlumberger maintains an interest rate risk management strategy that uses a mix of variable and fixed rate debt combined with its investment portfolio, to mitigate the exposure to changes in interest rates.&#160; </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At September 30, 2019, Schlumberger had fixed rate debt aggregating $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000853" name="slb:FixedRateDebt" contextRef="C_0000087347_20190930" decimals="-8" scale="9">14.0</ix:nonFraction> billion and variable rate debt aggregating $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000854" name="slb:VariableRateDebt" contextRef="C_0000087347_20190930" decimals="-8" scale="9">2.7</ix:nonFraction> billion. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Foreign Currency Exchange Rate Risk </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As a multinational company, Schlumberger generates revenue in more than <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbCountry" id="F_000855" name="us-gaap:NumberOfCountriesInWhichEntityOperates" contextRef="C_0000087347_20190930" decimals="INF">120</ix:nonFraction> countries. Schlumberger&#8217;s functional currency is primarily the US dollar.&#160; However, outside the United States, a significant portion of Schlumberger&#8217;s expenses are incurred in foreign currencies.&#160; Therefore, when the US dollar weakens (strengthens) in relation to the foreign currencies of the countries in which Schlumberger conducts business, the US dollar-reported expenses will increase (decrease).&#160;&#160; </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is exposed to risks on future cash flows to the extent that the local currency is not the functional currency and expenses denominated in local currency are not equal to revenues denominated in local currency.&#160;&#160;&#160; Schlumberger uses foreign currency forward contracts to provide a hedge against a portion of these cash flow risks.&#160; These contracts are accounted for as cash flow hedges, with the changes in the fair value of the hedge recorded on the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Balance Sheet </span>and in <span style="font-style:italic;">Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss.&#160; </span>Amounts recorded in<span style="font-style:italic;"> Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss </span>are reclassified into earnings in the same period or periods that the hedged item is recognized in earnings.&#160; </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is also exposed to risks on future cash flows relating to certain of its fixed rate debt denominated in currencies other than the functional currency. Schlumberger uses cross-currency swaps to provide a hedge against these cash flow risks. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During 2017, a Canadian-dollar functional currency subsidiary of Schlumberger issued $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000856" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentCarryingAmount" amount of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000857" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" <p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: <p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is exposed to changes in the fair value of assets and liabilities that are denominated in currencies other than the functional currency.&#160; While Schlumberger uses foreign currency forward contracts and foreign currency options to economically hedge this exposure as it relates to certain currencies, these contracts are not designated as hedges for accounting purposes.&#160; Instead, the fair value of the contracts is recorded on the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Balance Sheet, </span>and changes in the fair value are recognized in the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Statement of Income (Loss) </span>as are changes in fair value of the hedged item. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At September 30, 2019, contracts were outstanding for the US dollar equivalent of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000874" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapDerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis_us-gaapForeignExchangeContractMember_20190930" decimals="INF" scale="9">6.8</ix:nonFraction> billion in various foreign currencies, of which $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000875" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapDerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis_us-gaapForeignExchangeContractMember_us-gaapFinancialInstrumentAxis_us-gaapDebtMember_us-gaapHedgingDesignationAxis_us-gaapDesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember_20190930" decimals="INF" scale="9">2.8</ix:nonFraction> billion relates to hedges of debt denominated in currencies other than the functional currency. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At September 30, 2019, Schlumberger recognized a cumulative $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000876" name="us-gaap:ForeignCurrencyCashFlowHedgeGainLossReclassifiedToEarningsNet" contextRef="C_0000087347_20190101_20190930" decimals="-6" scale="6">37</ix:nonFraction> million loss in <span style="font-style:italic;">Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss</span> relating to changes in the fair value of foreign currency forward contracts and cross-currency swaps.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">15</p>

<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">Charges and credits are described in detail in Note 2 to the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Financial Statements.</span></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Third-quarter revenue of $8.5 billion increased 3% sequentially with North America revenue of $2.8 billion increasing 2%, while international revenue of $5.6 billion increased 3%.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">International revenue increased 3% sequentially, led by Europe/CIS/Africa where revenue increased 9% sequentially driven by the peak summer activity campaigns in the Northern Hemisphere as well as the start of new projects in Africa. Sequential international revenue growth was also driven by double-digit growth in Asia. Latin America revenue decreased 9% sequentially on lower activity in Argentina and Mexico.&#160; International activity in the fourth quarter will be affected by the usual winter slowdown, particularly in the Northern Hemisphere.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">North America revenue improved 2% sequentially, driven by WesternGeco<sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup> multiclient seismic license sales.&#160;&#160;Land revenue was slightly higher as a modest increase in OneStim<sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup> activity was off-set by softer pricing while land drilling revenue was essentially flat despite the lower rig count. As Schlumberger exited the third quarter, OneStim activity decelerated as frac programs were either deferred or cancelled due to customer budget and cash flow constraints.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The third quarter&#8217;s results reflected a macro environment of slowing production growth rate in North American land as operators maintained capital discipline and reduced drilling and frac activity. Year-to-date high single-digit international revenue growth continues to be underpinned by international investment levels. Market uncertainty, however, is weighing on future oil demand outlook in a climate where trade concerns are seen as challenging global economic growth.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Characterization </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Characterization revenue of $1.7 billion increased 6% sequentially due to peak summer activity campaigns. Growth was led by Wireline international activity, increased Integrated Service Management (ISM) project activity in India and higher WesternGeco multiclient seismic license sales in North America.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Characterization pretax operating margin of 22% was 149 basis points (bps) higher sequentially due to the peak summer campaign for Wireline and stronger WesternGeco multiclient seismic license sales.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">20</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Drilling </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Drilling revenue of $2.5 billion increased 2% sequentially led by stronger international activity in Russia from the peak summer drilling campaign that mainly benefited Drilling &#38; Measurements. Higher drilling activity in China and Australia also contributed to the sequential growth. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Drilling pretax operating margin of 12% was essentially flat sequentially. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production revenue of $3.2 billion increased 2% sequentially, primarily driven by higher international activity for Completions in the Far East, Asia &#38; Australia, Russia &#38; Central Asia, and Sub-Sahara Africa GeoMarkets.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Recent production shut-ins in Ecuador due to the ongoing civil unrest may potentially impact fourth quarter revenue.&#160; </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production pretax operating margin of 9% expanded 148 bps sequentially largely due to improved international margins from higher activity. Additionally, the reduction in depreciation and amortization expense as a result of the third quarter 2019 impairment charges (see Note 2 - <span style="font-style:italic;">Charges &#38; Credits</span>) accounted for just under half of the sequential margin improvement.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cameron </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cameron revenue of $1.4 billion increased 3% sequentially driven by higher international revenue for Surface Systems, OneSubsea, and Drilling Systems. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cameron pretax operating margin of 13% was essentially flat sequentially.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Third-quarter 2019 revenue of $8.5 billion was essentially flat year-on-year as North America revenue declined 11% while international revenue increased 8%. The international results were underpinned by increased investment levels. In contrast, the North America results reflect a slowing production growth rate on land as operators maintained capital discipline and reduced drilling and frac activity. </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">21</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Characterization </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Third-quarter 2019 revenue of $1.7 billion was 4% higher year-on-year. Revenue in Wireline, Testing, and ISM drove the increase as a result of higher international activity. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 90 bps to 22%. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Drilling </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Third-quarter 2019 revenue of $2.5 billion increased 2% year-on-year primarily due to higher demand for drilling services, largely in the international markets.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 161 bps to 12% despite higher revenue as margins were affected by competitive pricing and higher costs associated with a number of integrated contracts internationally.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Third-quarter 2019 revenue of $3.2 billion decreased 3% year-on-year with most of the revenue decrease attributable to lower OneStim activity in North America as customers reduced spending due to higher cost of capital, lower borrowing capacity and expectation of better returns from their shareholders. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 72 bps to 9% primarily due to reduced profitability in OneStim in North America.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cameron </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Third-quarter 2019 revenue of $1.4 billion decreased 2% year-on-year due to lower revenue for OneSubsea and Valves &#38; Process Systems.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin increased 117 bps to 13% due to improved profitability in OneSubsea. </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Nine Months 2019 Compared to Nine Months 2018</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nine-month 2019 revenue of $24.7 billion was essentially flat year-on-year with North America revenue decreasing 8% and international revenue increasing 6%. The international results were underpinned by increased investment levels. In contrast, the North America results reflect a slowing production growth rate on land as operators maintained capital discipline and reduced drilling and frac activity. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Characterization </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nine-month 2019 revenue of $4.7 billion increased 1% year-on-year primarily driven by increased international activity. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 91 bps to 20%.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Drilling </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nine-month 2019 revenue of $7.3 billion increased 7% year-on-year primarily due to higher demand for drilling services, largely in the international markets that benefited Drilling &#38; Measurements, M-I SWACO, and Integrated Drilling Services (IDS).</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 103 bps to 12% despite higher revenue as margins were affected by competitive pricing and  higher costs associated with a number of integrated contracts internationally.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nine-month 2019 revenue of $9.1 billion decreased 4% year-on-year with most of the revenue decline attributable to lower OneStim activity in North America as customers reduced spending due to higher cost of capital lower, borrowing capacity and expectation of better returns from their shareholders. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 90 bps to 8% primarily due to reduced profitability in OneStim in North America. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cameron </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nine-month 2019 revenue of $3.9 billion decreased 5% year-on-year due to lower revenue for OneSubsea and Valves &#38; Process Systems.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 19 bps to 12%. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Interest and Other Income</span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The effective tax rate for the first nine months of 2019 was 4%, as compared to 18% for the same period of 2018. The charges described in Note 2 to the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Financial Statements</span> reduced the effective tax rate for the first nine months of 2019 by 12 percentage points, as the majority of the charges related to non-deductible goodwill. </p>

Management believes that free cash flow is an important liquidity measure for the company and that it is useful to investors and management as a measure of our ability to generate cash.&#160;&#160;Once business needs and obligations are met, this cash can be used to reinvest in the company for future growth or to return to shareholders through dividend payments or share repurchases.&#160;&#160;Free cash flow does not represent the residual cash flow available for discretionary expenditures.&#160;&#160;Free cash flow is a non-GAAP financial measure that should be considered in addition to, not as substitute for or superior to, cash flow from operations. </p></td></tr></table></div>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of September 30, 2019, Schlumberger had $2.3 billion of cash and short-term investments on hand.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger had separate committed debt facility agreements aggregating $6.5 billion that support commercial paper programs, of which $4.1 billion was available and unused.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger believes these amounts are sufficient to meet future business requirements for at least the next 12 months. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Borrowings under the commercial paper programs at September 30, 2019 were $2.4 billion.</p>

Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">For quantitative and qualitative disclosures about market risk affecting Schlumberger, see Item&#160;7A, &#8220;Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk,&#8221; of the Schlumberger Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December&#160;31, 2018. Schlumberger&#8217;s exposure to market risk has not changed materially since December&#160;31, 2018.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="Item_4_Controls_and_Procedures"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Item&#160;4. Controls and Procedures. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger has carried out an evaluation under the supervision and with the participation of Schlumberger&#8217;s management, including the Chief Executive Officer (&#8220;CEO&#8221;) and the Chief Financial Officer (&#8220;CFO&#8221;), of the effectiveness of Schlumberger&#8217;s &#8220;disclosure controls and procedures&#8221; (as such term is defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;)) as of the end of the period covered by this report. Based on this evaluation, the CEO and the CFO have concluded that, as of the end of the period covered by this report, Schlumberger&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures were effective to provide reasonable assurance that information required to be disclosed in the reports that Schlumberger files or submits under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the Securities and Exchange Commission&#8217;s rules and forms. Schlumberger&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures include controls and procedures designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed in reports filed or submitted under the Exchange Act is accumulated and communicated to its management, including the CEO and the CFO, as appropriate, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure. There was no change in Schlumberger&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting during the quarter to which this report relates that has materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, Schlumberger&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">PART II. OTHER INFORMATION </span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">None<span style="font-weight:bold;">. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="Item_4_Mine_Safety_Disclosures"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Item&#160;4. Mine Safety Disclosures. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our mining operations are subject to regulation by the federal Mine Safety and Health Administration under the Federal Mine Safety and Health Act of 1977. Information concerning mine safety violations or other regulatory matters required by section 1503(a) of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act and Item&#160;104 of Regulation S-K is included in Exhibit 95 to this report.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="Item_5_Other_Information"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Item&#160;5. Other Information. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In 2013, Schlumberger completed the wind down of its service operations in Iran. Prior to this, certain non-US subsidiaries provided oilfield services to the National Iranian Oil Company and certain of its affiliates (&#8220;NIOC&#8221;).</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger&#8217;s residual transactions or dealings with the government of Iran during the third quarter of 2019 consisted of payments of taxes and other typical governmental charges. Certain non-US subsidiaries of Schlumberger maintain depository accounts at the Dubai branch of Bank Saderat Iran (&#8220;Saderat&#8221;), and at Bank Tejarat (&#8220;Tejarat&#8221;) in Tehran and in Kish for the deposit by NIOC of amounts owed to non-US subsidiaries of Schlumberger for prior services rendered in Iran and for the maintenance of such amounts previously received. One non-US subsidiary also maintained an account at Tejarat for payment of local expenses such as taxes. Schlumberger anticipates that it will discontinue dealings with Saderat and Tejarat following the receipt of all amounts owed to Schlumberger for prior services rendered in Iran.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">28</p>

<p style="text-align:right;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Exhibit 10.1</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="text-decoration:underline;">EMPLOYMENT, NON-COMPETITION AND </font></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="text-decoration:underline;">NON-SOLICITATION AGREEMENT</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:8.33%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_DV_M1"></a><a name="_DV_M2"></a>THIS <font style="font-weight:bold;">EMPLOYMENT, NON-COMPETITION AND NON-SOLICITATION</font> AGREEMENT (&#8220;Agreement&#8221;) is effective as of August 1<sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">st</sup>, 2019, by and between <font style="font-weight:bold;">SCHLUMBERGER LIMITED</font>, a Cura&#231;ao corporation (the &#8220;Company&#8221;), and Paal Kibsgaard <a name="_DV_M2"></a>(&#8220;Executive&#8221;).</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:8.33%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_DV_C4"></a><a name="_DV_M3"></a>1.<font style="margin-left:36pt;"></font><font style="text-decoration:underline;">Employment of Executive</font>:&nbsp;&nbsp;In consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements herein contained, including Executive&#8217;s execution of a release of claims as provided in as <font style="text-decoration:underline;">Exhibit A</font> to this Agreement, the Company and Executive enter into an agreement retaining Executive&#8217;s services as described herein, securing Executive&#8217;s covenants herein, <a name="_DV_C4"></a>establishing certain<a name="_DV_M3"></a> incentive,<font style="color:#000000;"> tenure and performance criteria related to such employment, and otherwise fixing Executive&#8217;s benefits.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:8.33%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_DV_M4"></a>2.<font style="margin-left:36pt;"></font><font style="text-decoration:underline;">Term and Extent of Services</font>: The term will commence August 1, 2019 (the &#8220;Effective Date&#8221;) and will continue until the close of business on July 31, 2022 (the &#8220;Term&#8221;). This Agreement does not constitute a guarantee of continued employment but instead provides for certain obligations of, and rights and benefits for, Executive during the Term, and in the event his employment with the Company terminates under the circumstances described herein.&nbsp;&nbsp;Effective as of August 1, 2019, Executive shall resign from his positions as Chairman of the Board and as Chief Executive Officer of the Company. Executive will remain employed by the Company through the end of the Term, unless otherwise terminated under Section 4.&nbsp;&nbsp;During the Term, the Executive shall be employed as an advisor reporting to the Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company (the &#8220;Board&#8221;). <font style="color:#000000;">At the expiration of the Term, Executive&#8217;s employment with the Company and all of its affiliates shall terminate.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_DV_M5"></a><a name="_DV_C5"></a><a name="_DV_M6"></a><a name="_DV_M7"></a>Nothing<a name="_DV_C5"></a> <a name="_DV_M6"></a>herein shall prohibit Executive, during the Term, from being engaged as a consultant or employee to organizations and businesses or to be appointed to their board of directors <a name="_DV_M7"></a>except those specifically identified as Unauthorized Competitors in Section 5.&nbsp;&nbsp;Executive agrees that he will not accept employment with any oil and gas related company without prior written approval from the Chairman of the Board.&nbsp;&nbsp;<font style="color:#000000;">For the avoidance of doubt, &#8220;oil and gas related company&#8221; expressly excludes any Unauthorized Competitor.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;"><a name="_DV_M8"></a>&nbsp;</p>

By way of illustration but not limitation, Confidential Information includes trade secrets, processes, formulas, know-how, improvements, discoveries, developments, designs, inventions, techniques, marketing plans, manual, records of research, reports, memoranda, computer software, strategies, forecasts, new products, unpublished financial statements or parts thereof, budgets or other financial information, projections, licenses, prices, costs, and employee, customer and supplier lists or parts thereof.</p></td></tr></table></div>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;"><a name="_DV_M67"></a><a name="_DV_M68"></a>&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">or to such other address as either party may furnish to the other in writing in accordance herewith, except that notices of changes of address shall be effective only upon receipt.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">9</a></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:8.33%;color:#000000;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_DV_M69"></a><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU10"></a><font style="color:#000000;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">8.</font><font style="margin-left:36pt;"></font><font style="text-decoration:underline;">Applicable Law; Venue</font><font style="color:#000000;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">: The validity, interpretation, construction and performance of this Agreement will be governed exclusively by and construed in accordance with the substantive laws of the State of Texas, without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws of such state.&nbsp;&nbsp;Any suit, action or other legal proceeding arising out of this Agreement shall be brought in the United States District Court for the Southern District of Texas, Houston Division, or, if such court does not have jurisdiction or will not accept jurisdiction, in any court of general jurisdiction in Harris County, Texas.&nbsp;&nbsp;Each of Executive and the Company consents to the jurisdiction of any such court in any such suit, action, or proceeding and waives any objection that it may have to the laying of venue of any such suit, action, or proceeding in any such court.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:8.33%;color:#000000;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_DV_M70"></a>9.<font style="margin-left:36pt;"></font><font style="text-decoration:underline;">Severability</font>: If a court of competent jurisdiction determines that any provision of this Agreement is invalid or unenforceable, then the invalidity or unenforceability of any other provision of this Agreement, and all other provisions shall remain in full force and effect.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:8.33%;color:#000000;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_DV_M71"></a>10.<font style="margin-left:36pt;"></font><font style="text-decoration:underline;">Withholding of Taxes</font>: The Company may withhold from any benefits payable under this Agreement all federal, state, city or other taxes as may be required pursuant to any law or governmental regulation or ruling.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:8.33%;color:#000000;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_DV_M72"></a>11.<font style="margin-left:36pt;"></font><font style="text-decoration:underline;">No Assignment; Successors</font>: Executive&#8217;s right to receive payments or benefits hereunder shall not be assignable or transferable, whether by pledge, creation, or a security interest or otherwise, whether voluntary, involuntary, by operation of law or otherwise, other than as provided in Section 4(a), a transfer by will or by the laws of descent or distribution, and in the event of any attempted assignment or transfer contrary to this Section 11, the Company shall have no liability to pay any amount so attempted to be assigned or transferred.&nbsp;&nbsp;This Agreement shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by Executive&#8217;s personal or legal representatives, executors, administrators, successors, heirs, distributes, devises and legatees.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_DV_M73"></a>This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the Company, its successors and assigns (including, without limitation, any company into or with which the Company may merge or consolidate).</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:8.33%;color:#000000;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_DV_M74"></a>12.<font style="margin-left:36pt;"></font><font style="text-decoration:underline;">Effect of Prior Agreements</font>: This Agreement contains the entire understanding between the parties hereto and supersedes any prior employment, severance or other agreement between the Company or any predecessor of the Company and Executive; except that (i) this Agreement will not affect or reduce any benefit or compensation inuring to Executive of a kind elsewhere expressly provided and not modified in this Agreement, and is not intended to modify the terms and conditions of the award agreements or plans governing the terms of Executive&#8217;s equity compensation awards and (ii) any restrictive covenants included in prior arrangements with the Company or its Affiliates that impose additional or broader requirements or restrictions on Executive remain in effect in accordance with their terms.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">10</a></p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:8.33%;color:#000000;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">14.<font style="margin-left:36pt;"></font><font style="text-decoration:underline;">Section 409A</font>:&nbsp;&nbsp;Each payment under this Agreement, including each payment in a series of installment payments, is intended to be a separate payment for purposes of Treas. Reg. &#167; 1.409A-2(b), and is intended to be: (i) exempt from Section 409A of the Code, the regulations and other binding guidance promulgated thereunder (&#8220;Section 409A&#8221;), including, but not limited to, by compliance with the short-term deferral exemption as specified in Treas. Reg. &#167; 1.409A-1(b)(4) and the involuntary separation pay exception within the meaning of Treas. Reg. &#167; 1.409A-1(b)(9)(iii), or (ii) in compliance with Section 409A, including, but not limited to, being paid pursuant to a fixed schedule or specified date pursuant to Treas. Reg. &#167; 1.409A-3(a) and the provisions of this Agreement will be administered, interpreted and construed accordingly.&nbsp;&nbsp;Notwithstanding the foregoing provisions of this Agreement, if the payment of any severance compensation or severance benefits under Section 2 would be subject to additional taxes and interest under Section 409A because the timing of such payment is not delayed as provided in Section 409A(a)(2)(B)(i) of the Code, and Executive constitutes a specified employee within the meaning of Section 409A(a)(2)(B)(i) of the Code, then any such payments that Executive would otherwise be entitled to during the first six months following Executive&#8217;s separation from service within the meaning of Section 409A(a)(2)(A)(i) of the Code shall be accumulated and paid on the date that is six months after Executive&#8217;s separation from service (or if such payment date does not fall on a business day of the Company, the next following business day of the Company), or such earlier date upon which such amount can be paid under Section 409A without being subject to such additional taxes and interest. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:8.33%;color:#000000;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">15.<font style="margin-left:36pt;"></font><font style="text-decoration:underline;">No Waiver</font>:&nbsp;&nbsp;No failure by either party hereto at any time to give notice of any breach by the other party of, or to require compliance with, any condition or provision of this Agreement shall be deemed a waiver of similar or dissimilar provisions or conditions at the same or at any prior or subsequent time.</p>
